description: Vectors of the schemas of structure version 1 (docs/api-stability.md, section 9), chapters 1 and 2: what is signed and what travels, and what is kept. Built by tests/schema_vectors.py with tests/schema_reference.py; tests/vectors/kern/profile_check.go checks them with tables of its own (-schemas). `accepted` holds objects that are of their schema on the network `network_id`. `refused` holds objects that are not: an accepted object (`from`) with members removed (`remove`), then values put in place (`set`), or an object of its own; `rule` names the rule that refuses it, by a key of `rules`. A path is names of members and positions in lists joined by full stops; a value put one position past the end of a list is added to it, and a position that is removed takes its item out of the list. Objects are written with the `directives`. `bytes` is the length of the canonical encoding of the object once its directives are carried out, and `pin` the first 8 bytes of the SHA3-384 of that encoding: they only show that two programs built the same object. The fillers are not keys, and no signature here verifies: a schema does not verify signatures. `mutations`, where present, asks for more: every object one change away from this one is refused, except this one without a member listed in `optional`. The changes: every array and every object replaced by the string x, and nothing more in the ones listed in `free`; elsewhere, every member of an object removed in turn, and a member zz of value 0 added, except in the objects listed in `maps`; every string replaced by 0, every boolean by 1, every integer by its digits as a string, then by true. `accepted_texts` and `refused_texts` are texts as a node receives them: the size of a frame and the nesting are checked on the bytes, then the canonical encoding, then the schema; the schema `json` is any value of canonical JSON, and `prefix` is the four bytes that precede the text in a frame. An accepted object of the schema `frame` has its `prefix` too: the length of its canonical encoding, most significant byte first, and nothing else. `prefixes` holds four bytes as a node reads them before a frame: `announces` is the number of bytes that follow, and `rule` refuses those that announce more than `frame_bytes`, which bounds what follows and does not count the four bytes. `answers` holds what a node sends in answer to a `get_blocks` from `from` to `to`: `held` lists the blocks it holds, each as a level and the bytes of its final block in the frame, and `levels` the levels of the blocks of its answer; a frame without a block is 29 bytes, and each block after the first adds a comma. `replies` holds answers as the node that asked sees them, by the levels of their blocks: accepted, or refused by `rule`. Chapter 2. A state is checked on itself, and a genesis on the network it names. `breaks`, on a refused state, account or genesis, is the sentence of the document that the object breaks, and it breaks no other: without that sentence the object is accepted. A state comes with its `state_root`, computed by the function it names, and with the root of its accounts, `accounts_root`; `state_full` comes with its `accounts` too, as the state trie holds them. A genesis comes with the nine fields of its block of level 0 in canonical JSON (`hashed`) and with the hash of that block (`block_hash`); a text of the schema `genesis` is read like any text, without a bound on its length. `charges` holds blocks of transfers: `state` gives the `chain_id`, the `parameters`, the `balances` and the `nonces` before the block, and `then` what the block leaves, with the positions of the transfers that failed and paid (`failed`); or `rule` names, by a key of `block_rules`, the rule that makes the block invalid, and `at` the position of the transaction that breaks it. `decisions` holds proposals that are decided at one level: `before` gives the parameters, the function of the state root, what the treasury holds (`treasury`) and the two bonds; a protocol proposal is its `payload` and whether its vote passes, and a treasury proposal the phase that ends, `voting` or `passed`, and when its vote ends whether it passes; `then` gives the phase each one is in afterwards and what the rest has become, with what was burned. `payments` holds transactions of guardians in one block: `before` gives the level of the block, the guardians, what the treasury holds, the bond of the treasury track, the delay of the guardians other than the first, and the treasury proposals by identifier, each one its `phase` as the block finds it, the level at which its vote ended (`voted`), the sum of its amounts (`total`), the part of that sum whose recipient is the treasury itself (`to_itself`) and `released_by` where a guardian has released it; an operation is its `sender`, its `kind` and the `proposal_id` it names; `then` gives what each operation did (`did`: `paid`, `recorded` or `cancelled`, or the rule that makes it fail, by a key of `guardian_rules`: the first one broken, in the order of that table), what the treasury holds, what was burned and each payment afterwards. Guardians, senders and identifiers are short names there: the rules only compare them. `rewards` holds the reward of a block: `before` gives `total_supply`, the address of the treasury, the five parameters the reward reads, the validators with their stakes and the delegations, each one its validator and its amount; `then` gives what is staked, the rate, the reward, what each address receives (`credits`) and `total_supply` afterwards. `tallies` holds votes: the weights of a snapshot (`consensus_set`), the vote of each validator that voted (`ballots`) and the track; `then` gives the weights of the yes and of the no, that of all the validators, whether the vote reaches its quorum and whether it passes. `slashes` holds the reports of offences of one block: `before` gives the level of the block, `delegation_unbonding_blocks` and the tables a slash reads, the proposals of the protocol track (`protocol`) as their `proposal_id` and their `double_votes`, and a vote of the consensus without its signature; an operation is its `sender`, its `kind` and its `params`; `then` gives what each operation did (`did`: `slashed`, or the rule that makes it fail, by a key of `slash_rules`: the first one broken, in the order of that table), what each address receives, what was burned and the tables afterwards. Addresses, identifiers and hashes are short names in these three families. `transitions` holds whole blocks on whole states: `from` names the state, an accepted vector or the result of an earlier transition (`name`), and `block` is an object of the schema `block`; `then` gives the state the block leads to as the members to remove from the first state (`remove`) and the values to put in place (`set`), the positions of the transactions whose operation failed (`failed`), the root of that state (`state_root`, which is the one in the header of the block) and the pin of its canonical encoding; or `rule` names what makes the block invalid, by a key of `whole_block_rules`, of `block_rules` or of `key_rules`, and `at` the position of the transaction that breaks it. `first_transactions` holds the transactions of one block as the key registry sees them: `before` gives the level of the block and `keys`; `then` gives the registry afterwards, or `rule` names, by a key of `key_rules`, the rule that makes the block invalid, the first one broken in the order of that table, and `at` the position of the transaction that breaks it. The fillers 300, 338, 356, 359 and 422 have an Ed25519 part that passes the check of the note; 301 has one that is no point of the curve, and 305 one that is a point outside the subgroup of prime order. `delegations`, `proposals` and `attestations` hold the operations of one block, for three families of kinds: `before` gives the level of the block and the tables the operations read and write, with `delegation_unbonding_blocks` for the first family and the two bonds for the second; an operation is its `sender`, its `kind`, its `params` where its kind has some, its `amount` where it moves one, and its `nonce` for an `attest`; `then` gives what each operation did (`did`: `delegated` or `ended`, `submitted` or `voted`, `attested` or `revoked`, or the rule that makes it fail, by a key of `delegating_rules`, `proposing_rules` or `attesting_rules`: the first one broken, in the order of its table) and the tables afterwards. Addresses are short names in these three families, and so are the identifiers a state already holds; the identifier of a proposal or of an attestation that an operation records is computed on the network of the file. `contracts` holds the originations and the calls of one block, as whole transactions on addresses of the network: `before` gives `balances` and `contracts`, and `then` what each transaction did (`originated`, `called`, or a key of `contract_rules`) and the two tables afterwards. Neither program has an interpreter of the language: `language` gives, under the position of each transaction that asks, what the language says of it. For an `originate`: `declares`, the fields of its code with their types, absent when the language refuses the code; `receives`, what the check of its invariants is given (`sender`, `amount`, `self`, `balance` and `storage`); `holds`, whether they hold. For a `call`: `takes`, the parameters of its entry point with their types, absent when the contract has no such entry point; `receives`, what its execution is given; `leaves`, the storage it leaves, absent when it fails. A program builds what an execution receives and finds it equal to `receives`; a position says nothing that is not asked, and a transaction of which nothing is asked has no position. A transition that creates or calls a contract has its `language` too. `exchanges` holds what happens on a connection as the node that asks for blocks sees it: a step is a request it would send (`ask`: the first and the last level), a `blocks` frame it receives (`blocks`: the levels of its blocks) or four bytes it reads before a frame (`prefix`); `verdicts` gives `accepted`, `refused` or `closed` for each step. `served` holds what a node sends when several requests reach it on one connection: `held` as in `answers`, and the levels of one answer for each request. The accepted objects of the schemas `rollup batch`, `inclusion request`, `Mini-EVM state` and `verifier key` are hashed outside blocks. Each comes with what the profile computes from it: the hash of a batch, taken without its signature (`hash`), and for the first one the text its sequencer signs and its context (`signed`, `context`); the hash of a request and of a state (`hash`); the identifier of a key (`id`).

rules.not_canonical: the bytes are not the canonical JSON of a value
rules.too_deep: arrays and objects are nested beyond the bound
rules.too_long: the encoding of a frame, a transaction, the transactions of a block or a claim is beyond its bound
rules.wrong_type: the value is not of the JSON type its schema gives
rules.unknown_field: the object has a member that its schema does not have
rules.missing_field: the object lacks a member that its schema requires
rules.out_of_range: an integer is outside its range, or a list or a map has too few or too many entries
rules.bad_text: a string is not one of the values allowed, or has a wrong length or a character outside its alphabet
rules.bad_address: a string is not an address of this network
rules.bad_key: a string is not the text form of a public key of scheme 1
rules.bad_signature: a string is not the text form of a signature of scheme 1
rules.inconsistent: a rule that ties several fields together is broken

block_rules.block_too_large: The sizes of its transactions add up to `max_block_bytes` at most.
block_rules.fee_under_floor: When `fee_floor_enabled` is `true`, the fee of each transaction is at least `fee_floor_base` plus `fee_floor_per_byte` times its size.
block_rules.wrong_chain: The `chain_id` of each transaction is the `chain_id` of the state.
block_rules.wrong_nonce: The `nonce` of each transaction is the nonce of its sender when its turn comes: the number of transactions of that sender applied before it. A sender whose nonce is 2^63 - 1 sends nothing more: its nonce could not go up.
block_rules.unpaid_fee: The sender of each transaction holds its `fee` when its turn comes.

guardian_rules.not_waiting: It names a proposal of the treasury track whose `phase` is `passed`.
guardian_rules.too_early: A guardian other than the first releases a payment in a block whose level is the end of `voting` plus `guardian_delay_blocks`, or higher.
guardian_rules.released_twice: A guardian other than the first releases a payment once.
guardian_rules.unfunded: A release that pays finds the sum of the amounts of the payment in the treasury. Otherwise it fails, and the payment goes on waiting.

slash_rules.no_double_vote: A `slash_equivocation` names a proposal of the protocol track on which its `equivocator` has a double vote that is not punished.
slash_rules.not_an_offence: The two votes of a `slash_consensus_equivocation` are of one validator, of one kind, of one level and of one round, and for two blocks.
slash_rules.not_a_validator: Their validator is a validator of the state.
slash_rules.not_yet: Their level is not above the level of the block.
slash_rules.too_old: Their level plus `delegation_unbonding_blocks` is not below the level of the block.
slash_rules.slashed_already: No slashed vote of the state is of that validator, kind, level and round.
slash_rules.not_two: A `slash_attestation_equivocation` names two attestations of the state, and not one of them twice.
slash_rules.no_contradiction: They are of one issuer, under one `schema_id` and about one `subject`, and their claims differ: their canonical JSON is not the same.
slash_rules.not_at_once: Neither was revoked before the other was issued.
slash_rules.nothing_to_take: The slash takes something: 1 mukrn at least, from a stake, a tranche or a bond.

whole_block_rules.wrong_level: The `level` of its header is the `level` of the state plus 1.
whole_block_rules.wrong_state_root: The `state_root` of its header is the root of the state the block leads to, computed by the function that state names.

key_rules.key_missing: A sender that has no key in `keys` carries its `public_key`.
key_rules.key_carried_again: A sender that has a key in `keys` carries none.
key_rules.key_of_another: The hash of the key a transaction carries is the address of its sender.
key_rules.not_a_key: That key passes the check the note makes of a key before it is recorded (its section 4.5, rule 4).
key_rules.key_known: No address has had that key.

delegating_rules.no_such_validator: A `delegate_stake` names a validator of the state.
delegating_rules.own_validator: That validator is not its sender.
delegating_rules.other_validator: Its sender has no delegation to another validator.
delegating_rules.no_delegation: The sender of an `undelegate_stake` has a delegation.
delegating_rules.release_out_of_range: The level at which that delegation is released, the level of the block plus `delegation_unbonding_blocks`, is not above 2^63 - 1.

proposing_rules.not_by_a_validator: A `governance_propose` of the protocol track is sent by a validator.
proposing_rules.known_proposal: No proposal of its track, in the state, has its identifier.
proposing_rules.crossed_rates: Its `params` do not hold an `i_min_ppm` above their `i_max_ppm`.
proposing_rules.bond_not_held: Its sender holds the bond of its track.
proposing_rules.voter_not_a_validator: A `governance_vote` is sent by a validator.
proposing_rules.unknown_proposal: It names a proposal of its `track`, in the state.
proposing_rules.vote_not_open: A vote of that proposal is open: its `phase` is `exploration` or `adoption` on the protocol track, `voting` on the treasury track.

attesting_rules.amount_not_held: The sender of an `attest` holds its `amount`.
attesting_rules.unknown_attestation: A `revoke_attestation` names an attestation of the state.
attesting_rules.not_the_issuer: Its sender is the issuer of that attestation.

contract_rules.code_refused: The language accepts the `code` of an `originate`: the code reads, none of its statements is more than 64 levels deep, and its types are right.
contract_rules.fields_out_of_bounds: That code declares 256 fields at most, each under a `name`.
contract_rules.undeclared_field: Every name of `initial_storage` is a field the code declares.
contract_rules.wrong_value: Every value of `initial_storage` is of the type of its field: an integer for `int`, `true` or `false` for `bool`, a text for `string`, an address of the network for `address`.
contract_rules.address_not_named: `initial_storage` names every field of the type `address`.
contract_rules.invariant_refused: The invariants of the contract hold on its first storage.
contract_rules.not_a_contract: The `recipient` of a `call` is the address of a contract.
contract_rules.payment_not_held: The sender of a `call` holds its `amount`.
contract_rules.wrong_parameters: `entry` is an entry point of that contract, and `params` names the parameters of that entry point, all of them and no other, each with a value of its type.
contract_rules.execution_refused: The execution succeeds: no `require` refuses, no value leaves the type `value`, the execution stays within its 10,000 steps and its 64 levels, and the invariants hold on the storage it leaves.

directives.$ref: the object of the accepted vector of that name, which stands earlier in the file
directives.$index: inside the item of a $list or of a $map, the number of the item, from 0, plus the argument; elsewhere, the argument
directives.$key: the text form of the 1,984 bytes SHAKE256('kern schema vectors, key N'), N being the argument in decimal
directives.$sig: the text form of the 3,373 bytes SHAKE256('kern schema vectors, signature N')
directives.$address: the address of this network whose hash is the 48 bytes SHAKE256('kern schema vectors, address N')
directives.$account: the address of the account whose public key is the key N of $key: the hash of that key (note, section 5)
directives.$key_of_parts: [n, m]: the text form of the first 1,952 bytes of the key n of $key, its ML-DSA part, followed by the last 32 bytes of the key m, its Ed25519 part
directives.$text: [count, piece]: the piece written count times
directives.$concat: [parts]: the parts one after the other, an integer in decimal
directives.$canonical: the canonical JSON of the argument, once its directives are carried out, as a text
directives.$list: [count, item]: a list of count items
directives.$map: [count, name, value]: an object of count members
